title: A Long Beach, California, tenant who lost an eviction jury trial with a lawyer used ChatGPT and Perplexity on appeal, and NBC News reported that she overturned the eviction, but court records show that her later petitions in the same case were denied in November 2025
summary: NBC News reported that Lynn White used ChatGPT and Perplexity to overturn her eviction on appeal; court records show that her later petitions in the case were denied in November 2025.
account: Lynn White, a small music production business owner living in a Long Beach, California, trailer park, was allegedly behind on rent and facing eviction. Represented by a lawyer from a local tenant advocacy network, she lost a jury trial. To appeal, she argued that Los Angeles Covid-era rules allowed a 12-month rent deferral. She gave her documents to ChatGPT and the AI search engine Perplexity. She used them to find procedural errors by the judge, to research the law and to draft her court responses. NBC News reported on 8 October 2025 that, after several months of litigation, she overturned the eviction. It said that she avoided roughly $55,000 in penalties and over $18,000 in overdue rent. NBC News gives no court, docket or ruling date for that result. Court of Appeal records show that on 5 November 2025 White, representing herself, petitioned the Court of Appeal, Second District, for a writ of mandate and a stay against the Los Angeles Superior Court and Judge Ronald F. Frank of the Long Beach courthouse. The petition concerned the same eviction case, 23LBUD01928, and the appellate division case 24APLC00165, with Best Trailer Park, LLC as the opposing party. The Court of Appeal denied the petition on 14 November 2025 and rejected a motion to vacate the denial on 17 November. The California Supreme Court allowed a late petition for review with a request for a stay and denied both on 26 November 2025 (S294091). A Community Note on an X post of 4 April 2026 cites these dockets.
purpose: ChatGPT is a general-purpose assistant for answering questions and drafting text. Perplexity is an AI search engine. Using them to research law, spot procedural errors and draft filings is within that general purpose. Neither is built as a legal service. The same NBC report documents litigants sanctioned for AI-invented case citations.
system: ChatGPT (paid plan, $20 a month) and Perplexity Pro ($20 a month)
model_version: Not reported; NBC News says White moved from the free ChatGPT tier to the $20-a-month plan and used Perplexity Pro, without naming model versions

ratings.reason: NBC News reported that she overturned the eviction and avoided roughly $55,000 in penalties and more than $18,000 in overdue rent. No cited source gives the ruling. Court records show that her later petitions in the same case were denied in November 2025.

ai_role.statement: White told NBC News that she gave ChatGPT her documents and case details. She said it and Perplexity identified procedural errors by the judge, researched the applicable law and drafted her court responses. She said she could never have won the appeal without AI. No court document, opposing-party or judicial account of what decided the appeal is cited. So the tools' contribution relative to the Covid-era rent-deferral rules she invoked and her own advocacy is not established.

fields.summary: NBC News reported that Lynn White used ChatGPT and Perplexity to overturn her eviction on appeal; court records show that her later petitions in the case were denied in November 2025.
fields.account: Lynn White, a small music production business owner living in a Long Beach, California, trailer park, was allegedly behind on rent and facing eviction. Represented by a lawyer from a local tenant advocacy network, she lost a jury trial. To appeal, she argued that Los Angeles Covid-era rules allowed a 12-month rent deferral. She gave her documents to ChatGPT and the AI search engine Perplexity. She used them to find procedural errors by the judge, to research the law and to draft her court responses. NBC News reported on 8 October 2025 that, after several months of litigation, she overturned the eviction. It said that she avoided roughly $55,000 in penalties and over $18,000 in overdue rent. NBC News gives no court, docket or ruling date for that result. Court of Appeal records show that on 5 November 2025 White, representing herself, petitioned the Court of Appeal, Second District, for a writ of mandate and a stay against the Los Angeles Superior Court and Judge Ronald F. Frank of the Long Beach courthouse. The petition concerned the same eviction case, 23LBUD01928, and the appellate division case 24APLC00165, with Best Trailer Park, LLC as the opposing party. The Court of Appeal denied the petition on 14 November 2025 and rejected a motion to vacate the denial on 17 November. The California Supreme Court allowed a late petition for review with a request for a stay and denied both on 26 November 2025 (S294091). A Community Note on an X post of 4 April 2026 cites these dockets.
